summary: Committed SmolLM2 evidence now localizes the next blocker to reference-compatible first-token diagnosis. The pinned artifact is reference-good under a raw SmolLM2 ChatML prompt, and the current Rust strict CPU retry reaches generation with fallback_used=false but selects token `The` for the math prompt. Existing committed evidence is insufficient to promote CPU answer readiness or start CUDA planning.

source_evidence.finding: Before the governed normalization exception, strict CPU loading failed closed at blk.0.ffn_norm.weight before tokenizer loading, prompt rendering, or generation.
Exact metadata-scoped SmolLM2 normalization validation was implemented while generic llama normalization validation remains fail-closed.
Strict CPU tokenizer, prompt rendering, and one-token generation were reached with fallback_used=false, but the math prompt selected token id 504 decoded as `The` instead of the expected answer `4`.
The same pinned artifact was reference-good under a raw SmolLM2 ChatML prompt for bounded math, capital, and Rust prompts.
Prior diagnostic probes matched prompt/token IDs for one prompt variant but still produced incoherent Rust output, so prompt/token parity alone was insufficient in that evidence set.

diagnosis.why_not_prompt_only: Committed M4 diagnostic evidence records a prompt/token-ID parity probe that still produced incoherent Rust output after the first reference token, so prompt/token parity alone cannot promote the model.
diagnosis.why_not_math_only: The latest strict CPU retry does not include a same-prompt reference first-token/top-k comparison, so this receipt cannot isolate the blocker to transformer math, LM-head logits, tokenizer policy, or prompt-template policy.
diagnosis.why_not_cuda: SmolLM2 has no CPU answer-ready proof; dense all-layer planning and strict CUDA one-token proof remain blocked until the CPU/reference comparator localizes or clears the wrong-first-token behavior.
